name: NASA TR R-100 config 82 (conical afterbody, fins excluded)
_notes: Stoney (1961), NASA TR R-100, Figure 13(a), PDF page 21; config sheets (e.g. 82 on PDF page 99). d = 1.50 in = 0.0381 m; l_N/d = 7.13; l_A/d = 1.78; r_b/R = 0.438; tabulated A_b/A_max = 0.19; tabulated theta_b = 9 deg. Rounded sheet area and angle are provenance, not independent geometry constraints; radii and lengths define the fixture.
Full parabolic nose: shape='parabolic', shapeParameter=1, r/R=2(x/l_N)-(x/l_N)^2. App shapeProfile.ts and OpenRocket Transition.Shape.PARABOLIC use (2u-p*u^2)/(2-p); p=1 gives the full parabola.
NO cylindrical midbody: the afterbody immediately follows the nose. NO fins: the real helium-gun models have three fins (1.8 in root, 45 deg sweep), but Figure 13(a) C_D,A excludes them.

Free flight, no sting; Re approximately 8-12 million based on model length. C_D,A is afterbody pressure plus base drag, excluding friction, so ISA sea-level scoring is acceptable. Polished finish and 1 mm wall are fixture assumptions, not measured drag inputs for this quantity.
Score pressure CD minus the same nose-only fixture's pressure CD, plus the full fixture's base CD. Reference area is the maximum body cross-section; refAreaScale=1.

Figure reads supplied in the assignment: mean of independent Claude and Gemini 300-dpi reads, uncertainty half their difference plus reading resolution. Informational only. Equation (1) is unresolved and is NOT used.
